scope: Part 3 of the noun/particle series: unchanged independently reviewed article and 50 exercises, after initial independent review and informed fresh-reviewer reconciliation. Local, not published.

sources.inspected: Complete actual HTML body, including examples omitted by simplified extraction. Sections II (mo), III (dake/bakari), V (shika), VII (demo), VIII (made), IX (sae), XI (case combinations).
sources.qualifications: The actual examples supply both ni-dake and dake-ni. Do not adopt a universal case-before or case-after rule. The source's parenthetical only-if gloss of conditional sae is not used as a necessary-condition logical definition; its actual examples describe sufficiency in context. Approximation, historical classifications and every marked combination are not new practice targets.

sources.inspected: Actual basic contrast, negative-form section, matched one-person negative examples, same-meaning/different-feeling discussion, and FAQ.
sources.qualifications: The article explicitly rejects obligatory disappointment. The authored sister/teacher contexts establish the compared set. Object-plus-dake negative scopes are not assigned one unrestricted interpretation.

authorReview.scope: Complete article; all 48 full exercise objects, 126 accepted renderings, 122 base options and eight additional options; all lexical occurrences, protected intervals and 31 canonical cards. Separate formation limits, whole-sentence polarity, context keys, option rationales, source-global relationships and answer-hint boundaries checked.
authorReview.meaningOfClean: No actionable defect established in this direct author pass; not independent confirmation, native-speaker certification or exhaustive correctness.
authoringDecisions: Use explicit subject-focused dake negatives against shika negatives; do not force a universal object-negative scope interpretation.
Retain both case-dake orders where the whole recipient/location task permits them. Named formation drills do not turn nomi, bakari or another inclusion family into generally invalid Japanese.

Use ability/generic-error contexts for broad shared inclusion rather than assuming scalar demo in every bare past-arrival report. Potential koraremasu is explicitly ability, not honorific reference; it does not report an actual arrival.

Include sae/desae, sura/desura, emphatic mo combinations, demo, conversational datte, made/mademo and plain mo in the two fitting shared tasks. Preserve style/framing differences in feedback and use only substantive variants as additional buttons.
Use books versus newspapers rather than rely on books and manga being mutually exclusive categories. The latter can overlap.

Invitation glosses give the lexical actions drink/read rather than assert factual nondrinking/nonreading. Polarity/ability/conditional and minimum-quantity units are protected when their interpretation is the target.

Explicit answer labels are not grammatical definitions. A quoted-sentence label remains outside the Japanese sentence; count tasks explicitly request an Arabic numeral, with fullwidth input covered by NFKC.
Recognized dake/made spellings are typed variants, not equally frequent beginner display forms. No new JLPT assignment, hard prerequisite or claim of exhaustive alternative wording.
limits: No independent reviewer or reconciliation was run for this draft; preceding article verdicts do not transfer.
Existing canonical cards were read fully for occurrence-level sense/reading evidence; this is not 31 new external dictionary lookups or a new review of every card's origin claims.

Some matched contexts deliberately recur across named formation and interpretation tasks. Eight groups and 24 group/facet assignments are organizational coverage, not 48 independent discourse situations.
Not a learning-outcome, native-frequency, all-dialect, exhaustive-paraphrase or physical-device validation claim.

article.correctness: No actionable linguistic defect established. The selected noun attachments, retained case relations, four negative predicate forms, subject-focused negative-scope contrasts, ability versus occurrence, additive versus scalar readings, endpoint versus emphatic まで, and sufficient-condition boundary are coherent. The text appropriately limits rather than universalizes the alternatives.
article.scopedCoverage: Issue #7's required restriction, polarity, unexpected inclusion, ordinary も, scope/register, selected particle combinations, and cross-references are present. こそ, advanced restriction/negation, and fuller conditional formation are explicitly deferred. An exhaustive particle syllabus is neither promised nor required.
article.comprehensibility: Contextual expectation is explained rather than encoded as a permanent ranking of people or particles. Matched negative and focus-position examples do demonstrate their stated contrasts. Selective readings cover the less transparent forms used by the article. No consequential unexplained attachment prerequisite was established.

exercises.correctness: The accepted answer classes and grading distinctions survived the bounded review; no accepted distractor or established missing in-scope completion was found. RII-F01 is a localized false statement in one distractor rationale, not an error in its answer key.
exercises.scopedCoverage: All 22 declared constructions are exercised. All eight groups own six exercises, with two distinct scene keys for each local facet. Required restriction, negative-scope, case-retention, inclusion and interpretation work is present. Transfer is more limited than the raw count of 48 might suggest, but this is not an established omission from the agreed introductory scope; see RII-O01 and RII-O03.
exercises.comprehensibility: Visible instructions distinguish formation restrictions from meaning tasks and define external answer labels. Explanations usually acknowledge alternatives correctly. RII-F01 creates an avoidable ability/actual-event contradiction; other template residue is nonblocking polish under RII-O02.

findings.preciseClaim: The wrong-option rationale for だけ says, 'This would exclude the other people who explicitly participated.' The visible scenario establishes that the schedule lets the friends come, not that they actually participated. With the explicitly stipulated potential reading, 先生だけ来られます would restrict who can come.
findings.learnerImpact: This locally converts ability into a completed event, contrary to the exercise's own final explanation and the article's ability/occurrence warning. A learner consulting the wrong-answer rationale receives a different truth-condition explanation from the main feedback. The answer remains correctly rejected, so the impact is limited.
findings.minimalSuggestedRemedy: Change the rationale to refer to the friends who can also come under the stated schedule, for example: 'This would say only the teacher can come, contradicting the friends' stated ability to come.' Do not change the accepted answer class.

inspectedEvidence.passage: Line 1693 explicitly says the predicate expresses ability, and line 1695 says that an ability claim about coming does not itself report an actual arrival.
The linked canonical words/来る.md identifies 来られる as a potential form; the prompt-specific gloss at lines 1770-1772 is 'can come'.
Section VII example (43), このアルバイトは、いそがしい人でもできます, presents inclusion in ability; it does not report that the person performed the job.

confidence.calibration: The inconsistency is explicit within the frozen object. Severity is minor because the prompt and main explanation already give the correct interpretation and no grading change is needed.

optional.observation: There are 16 explicitly named formation tasks, 30 interpretation tasks and only two broader contextual-completion tasks. Some formation tasks mostly rehearse a supplied particle, and several interpretation tasks can be answered by matching the supplied English scenario to an English-defined label. Book/water and teacher/child substitutions provide useful controlled repetition but limited evidence of transfer.
optional.suggestion: If later expansion is desired, replace or supplement a small number of these with less-cued, still bounded transfer tasks. A wallet/existence restriction or a fresh matched ability contrast could test generalization beyond buying, drinking and attendance. Keep all contextually fitting particles accepted rather than manufacturing a unique winner.
optional.whyNotDefect: Named formation drills are legitimate here; instructions are visible and do not falsely declare other constructions ungrammatical. The set also contains real polarity and scope contrasts. Issue #7 asks for covering introductory exercises with multiple contexts, not demonstrated production mastery or an unrestricted test of every particle.
optional.confidence: High for the task distribution and degree of cueing; actual learning transfer would require learner evidence.

optional.observation: Shared feedback retains material belonging to a paired scenario. The clearest example is the final sentence about an ability claim and actual arrival in the expert-friend error exercise. Other objects say 'reading/drinking', 'not coming either, or not eating fish either', or discuss both a station and five o'clock when only one appears in the current item.
optional.suggestion: Make each explanation refer first to its own sentence. If a cross-example comparison is useful, introduce it explicitly rather than leaving a template's other scenario unexplained.
optional.whyNotDefect: Apart from RII-F01, the retained statements are true comparisons or irrelevant reminders rather than established linguistic errors. They do not alter the answer keys or make the task unanswerable.
optional.confidence: High that the residue exists; its effect on comprehension is a modest editorial judgment.

optional.observation: The sufficient-condition explanations correctly distinguish sufficiency from unique necessity. The actual choice, however, contrasts sufficiency with an unexpected event having already happened. It does not independently test whether the learner understands the sufficiency/necessity distinction named in the facet label.
optional.suggestion: If that logical distinction is intended to be measured rather than merely explained, add a carefully bounded interpretation alternative about whether the sentence proves the absence of every other possible route.
optional.whyNotDefect: The article explicitly calls conditional さえ a recognition boundary and defers fuller formation. These two items do perform that recognition task. I do not read their descriptive facet label as a promise of an additional exhaustive contrast.
optional.confidence: High about what the current options test; tentative and nonblocking as a curriculum recommendation.

evidence.inspected: Sections II, III, V, VII, VIII, IX and XI, including the Japanese examples recovered from the actual HTML body.
passages: The しか section states that the predicate is negative and gives ジュースしかありません.
Examples (53) and (55) contrast 君にだけ話しましょう and 君だけに話しましょう.
The でも section gives お茶でも飲みませんか and an ability example with いそがしい人でもできます.
The まで and さえ sections add 山田さん to an already-mentioned set of arrivals.
The conditional section gives これさえあればだいじょうぶです.

evidence.qualification: The source's parenthetical English 'only if' in the conditional discussion was not adopted as a formal necessary-condition rule. Daijisen's explicit sufficiency definition is more precise for that issue. TUFS's general case-particle shortcut was also not treated as an unrestricted prohibition on all marked orders.

Explicitly says that しか does not always express unhappiness or disappointment.

answerReview.method: Every object was read in full. Each completion was assessed in the literal blank and the full visible task; interpretation labels were assessed as labels outside the quotation, not inserted into the quoted sentence. Every base and additional option and its rationale was read.
answerReview.formation: The named だけ, しか-negative, retained-case, さえ-family, でも and まで-family restrictions are legitimate visible restrictions. Other restriction particles, different verb registers, and arbitrary synonyms were not automatically required merely because they can express related meanings elsewhere.
answerReview.broadContexts: Both 15-rendering shared-inclusion classes were assessed with their own ability/error context. も can leave unexpectedness to that context; でも, さえ/でさえ, すら/ですら, だって and まで offer fitting framings here without becoming universal equivalents. Emphatic も and the recognized 迄 spellings were checked as part of those literal completions.
answerReview.interpretationLabels: Kana alternatives are supported where authored; the visible label tasks do not promise acceptance of arbitrary English translations, synonyms or alternative label spellings. No false rejection was established on that basis.
answerReview.options: The 122 base options contain one correct representative per object. All eight additional labels belong to their accepted classes. No normalized accepted-answer/distractor collision was found. RII-F01 concerns the wording of one rationale rather than its correctness as a distractor.

vocabularyReview.method: All 93 occurrence-specific spans were read alongside their own prompt and full object. All 220 exclusions were read with offsets, text and reason. An additional read-only check confirmed exact code-point slices, complete contiguous coverage by spans plus exclusions, and prompt hashes.
vocabularyReview.linguisticResult: No established reading, headword, sense, canonical-link or target-leakage defect was found. Repeated occurrences were checked separately, including both verbs in the positive-addition prompts. Inflected readings such as 来られます/こられます and 勉強できません/べんきょうできません fit their supplied context.
vocabularyReview.polarityAndProtectedMaterial: Outcome predicates and minimum counters are protected in the polarity/count interpretation tasks. Inflected lexical verbs are legitimately glossed in formation or scope tasks where they are not the tested missing material. The invitation glosses 'drink' and 'read' are contextual lexical help within ませんか, not assertions that the invitations have affirmative morphology.
vocabularyReview.canonicalIdentityResult: The 31 linked cards match the intended senses/readings: for example 家/いえ rather than a mechanical switch to うち, 本 as book rather than a long-object counter, 切符 as a travel ticket, and 勉強 as the study lexeme supporting its する/potential forms. Independent claims elsewhere in the cards were not newly audited.

referenceArticleContextRead.purpose: Existing ほか/しか and だけ/ばかり cross-reference destinations
Positive/negative も and retained case relations

checks.assessment: Builds restriction and interprets the named object's positive action. Book/water cases are controlled repetition rather than evidence of many independent constructions.
Sister attendance and teacher reading genuinely contrast だけ-negative with しか-negative. Not-only items include both named members without asserting an exhaustive inventory.
Recipient に and activity-location で give genuinely different roles. Both だけ orders are accepted; retained case relations are visible task requirements.

Matched teacher/child scenes practice named forms, not unique semantic selection between them. The two shared-answer scenes permit multiple framings and do not claim independent mastery of each accepted form.
Separates expected basic-case failure, ordinary negative addition and zero minimum count. Reading/writing, attendance/diet and person/occurrence counts supply more than one setting.
Arrival/error inclusion is distinguished from spatial/time endpoints. Paired formation and interpretation items correctly share their scene keys across facets.
Contexts explicitly establish ordinary addition, expectation-relative large amounts, or suggestions. The outgoing topic-inclusion link exists and concerns positive/negative addition.
Reading and drinking pairs genuinely change the restricted phrase. Ticket/time examples recognize conditional sufficiency, not full formation or an independent necessity test.

groupChecks.coverageQualification: The two scene keys per facet satisfy the bounded local context requirement on this reading of the contract. Several are deliberately parallel templates; different keys should not be interpreted as a validated measurement of generalization. No unwarranted app-level prerequisite was added.

reviewValue.concreteContribution: One small, reproducible ability-versus-actual-event inconsistency was identified in a wrong-answer rationale. Its remedy is local and does not require changing an answer class.
negativeResultsWorthPreserving: The article's scope and major linguistic contrasts survived the independent review.
No defect was established in the 126 accepted renderings, 93 vocabulary spans, 220 exclusions or 31 canonical vocabulary identities.
Recognized spellings and shared inclusion alternatives were checked without turning recognition into a frequency claim or treating a restricted formation task as an unrestricted synonym task.
Source qualifications were checked against actual relevant passages, including resolving missing Japanese extraction and avoiding several overbroad teaching shortcuts.
The exercise count was separated from the number of independently practiced distinctions; optional transfer concerns were not promoted into a manufactured coverage failure.
reviewValue.laterAssessment: Adjudicate RII-F01 on its text and truth conditions. Compare equivalent observations across findings, optional notes and limits before assigning novelty. Record whether the optional suggestions are useful for this introductory scope. This report alone does not establish unique model value or general model superiority.

dispositions.adjudication: Accepted as a minor correctness/comprehensibility defect. No edit has been applied.
dispositions.evidence: The context expressly makes the predicate an ability claim and the explanation denies an inference of actual arrival. The wrong-option rationale nevertheless says the other people explicitly participated.
dispositions.remedy: Explain that only the teacher can come would exclude the friends who can also come under the stated schedule. Keep the answer key and accepted forms unchanged.
dispositions.incrementalContribution: The author pass already understood ability versus occurrence but missed propagating its final scenario refinement into this distractor rationale. The new contribution is a specific consistency defect, not discovery of a new grammatical rule.

dispositions.adjudication: Useful pedagogical observation, not a coverage failure. The 16 formation, 30 interpretation and two broader contextual tasks are guided introductory practice; their count is not a measure of independent transfer.
dispositions.recommendation: Consider a few less-cued but still bounded transfer tasks rather than rewriting or expanding the whole set. Preserve fitting alternative answers.
dispositions.limits: No learner study establishes that more open-ended items would improve outcomes.

dispositions.adjudication: Worthwhile localized feedback polish. The expert-friend error explanation contains the unrelated reminder about ability to come versus actual arrival. Other paired explanations mention both scenarios without introducing the comparison.
dispositions.recommendation: Make feedback refer first to the current sentence; introduce cross-example comparisons deliberately rather than leaving shared-template residue.
dispositions.limits: Apart from F01, these observations do not establish an incorrect answer or false grammatical rule.

dispositions.adjudication: Correct distinction between explained and independently assessed knowledge. The conditional items contrast sufficiency with an already-occurred surprise, not sufficiency with necessity.
dispositions.recommendation: If independent assessment of sufficiency versus necessity is desired, add an appropriately bounded contrast. Do not retroactively claim the current recognition tasks already measure it.
dispositions.limits: The article explicitly promises a recognition boundary and defers full conditional practice; no required scope gap is established.

dispositions.rationale: The だけ rationale now says that only the teacher could come would contradict the friends' stated ability to come. It no longer invents actual participation. dispositions.confidence: High: the original inconsistency and its removal are explicit within the complete object.

dispositions.rationale: The adopted limited-transfer refinement is implemented. Refrigerator contents require choosing だけ rather than しか with printed affirmative あります. The wallet task gives しか but no instruction to choose NEGATIVE, so the learner must supply ありません from the complete restriction while interpreting five hundred yen as present, not absent. These are existence/cash applications rather than another buying, drinking or attendance substitution.
wholeObjectChecks: 冷蔵庫には水だけあります is coherent in the supplied food/drink inventory context. 水しかありません expresses a corresponding restriction but cannot replace the printed affirmative predicate. The explicit two-particle choice excludes unrelated synonyms and extra particles; だけ and its recognized 丈 spelling are supported.

財布には五百円しかありません fits the cash question, ordinary polite nonpast ます-series instruction and kana requirement. あります is unsuitable after printed しか. Other negative registers, a different verb or a heightened-polite expression are visibly outside the task, not falsely declared ungrammatical.
The wallet explanation correctly confines the amount to this wallet and does not infer dissatisfaction or inventory money elsewhere.
冷蔵庫 / れいぞうこ, 財布 / さいふ, 水 / みず and local 五百円 / ごひゃくえん have matching senses. あります and しか plus the blank are protected rather than glossed into polarity answers.
The new examples belong to the existing form-dake and form-shika facets, with new context keys and no new construction identity.
dispositions.qualification: Resolved means the useful optional recommendation was adopted, not that the earlier set was defective or that these guided tasks prove general production transfer. The task remains intentionally bounded; unrestricted synonym acceptance or empirical transfer evidence is not required.
dispositions.confidence: High for the authored task improvement and its linguistic coherence; no empirical learning-effect claim is made.

dispositions.rationale: The expert-friend item no longer ends with the unrelated arrival/ability reminder. Reading versus drinking, sibling absence versus diet, station versus five o'clock, waiting versus book quantities, and tea versus book invitations now each receive their own feedback. The teacher/child だけ explanations identify the relevant learners or adults, and shared-inclusion evidence names the current ability or error situation.
dispositions.regressionCheck: The replacements preserve nonpast versus past reading/drinking, ordinary negative addition, spatial versus temporal endpoints, expectation-relative quantity and negative-question invitation force. The remaining 'drink-style suggestion' comparison in the でも formation explanations is an explicit relevant contrast, not an unexplained carryover scenario. No new semantic contradiction was found.
dispositions.qualification: This closes an adopted nonblocking editorial refinement. It does not retroactively turn every original generic explanation into a correctness defect.
dispositions.confidence: High: all complete affected objects, not only replacement sentences, were inspected.

dispositions.rationale: Both questions now directly offer 唯一, defined as the sentence ruling out every alternative arrangement, beside 十分 and the already-happened surprise distractor. The English setup no longer first translates the Japanese as 'will be enough.' A learner must identify what the conditional sentence establishes rather than merely copy that scene paraphrase.
dispositions.semanticCheck: 切符さえあれば入れます and 時間さえあれば行けます present a sufficient condition under the settled background and a possible ability/result, not an event already accomplished. The sentences do not themselves inventory and reject every alternative arrangement. The revised rationale correctly says further information would be needed for that stronger exclusivity conclusion.
dispositions.necessityQualification: The item tests an asserted sufficient condition versus an unestablished exclusive-route inference. It does not assert that the stated condition can never also be necessary in a particular real situation, that someone can travel without time, or that an alternative route actually exists. The time question expressly leaves possible changes to arrangements undiscussed.
dispositions.cueingCheck: The word 'enough' remains in the definition of the 十分 response label, just as the competing labels have English definitions. That is necessary label support, not a pre-supplied translation of the Japanese sentence. This is still a guided recognition check, not a test of all necessary/sufficient-condition combinations or free conditional formation.
